subject: Fractions
curriculum_context: Ghanaian upper primary (B.S. 4-6), generated against a 10-node skill graph.
cultural_context: Ghanaian upper-primary / junior-high context. Use Ghana cedis (GH₵), Ghanaian names (Kofi, Ama, Akua, Kwame, Yaa, Esi), local foods (jollof, kelewele, plantain, watermelon), and market settings. Use slash notation (a/b) for fractions and unicode vulgar fractions (½, ⅓, ⅔, ¼, ¾) for mixed numbers.

skill_descriptions.Division: Dividing whole numbers with no remainder, up to 100/10.
skill_descriptions.Concept_of_fraction: Understanding a fraction a/b as a parts out of b equal parts of a whole.
skill_descriptions.Equivalent_fractions: Generating equivalent fractions by multiplying numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number.
skill_descriptions.Simplifying_fractions: Reducing a fraction to its simplest form by dividing numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor.
skill_descriptions.Mixed_to_improper: Converting a mixed number (whole + fraction) to an improper fraction.
skill_descriptions.Improper_to_mixed: Converting an improper fraction to a mixed number using division with remainder.
skill_descriptions.Multiplying_fractions: Multiplying two fractions by multiplying numerators and denominators, then simplifying.
skill_descriptions.PEDMAS: Applying order of operations (parentheses, exponents, multiplication, division) on chained fraction expressions.

design_notes: Items deliberately avoid relying on addition or subtraction of fractions since those nodes are absent from the user's DAG. A production version should add 'Add/subtract fractions' and 'Common denominator' nodes before generating PEDMAS items that mix +/- with x/÷.
All items are multiple-choice for paper administration and machine-checkable scoring. Distractors are aligned to named misconceptions from the misconceptions section where possible.
Currency uses Ghana Cedis (GH₵). Names and contexts use Ghanaian referents (Kofi, Ama, Akua, Kwame, Yaa, Esi; kelewele, jollof, plantain, watermelon, market settings).
Vulgar-fraction unicode characters (½, ⅓, ⅔, ¼, ¾, ⅕, ⅖, ⅗, ⅘) are used for mixed numbers; slash notation (a/b) for general fractions.
Each item has a distractor_rationales field giving the misconception each wrong option targets, useful both for review and for downstream misconception-level diagnosis beyond skill mastery.
